photo.alt: Mist on Dal Lake with shikaras at first light

past.body: Srinagar is a city of water and gardens in the Kashmir Valley, cradled by the Himalaya. Shalimar and Nishat Bagh step down the hillside in terraces of chinar trees, fountains and roses.

table.body: Visit old city workshops, then sit down to a Wazwan feast.

fieldNotes.body: Hire a shikara before sunrise to see the floating market, then drift past lotus beds and kingfishers.
fieldNotes.bestTime: April to October; December to February for snow
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Fly into Srinagar airport, or take the train via Katra

photo.alt: First sun on the Pir Panjal ridgeline above Manali

past.body: Manali sits at the top of the Kullu Valley, where the Beas river meets snow peaks and cedar forests. Hadimba Temple is a wooden shrine with tiered roofs, hidden in a forest of giant deodar cedars.

fieldNotes.body: Drive towards Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel for snow, even when the town is green.
fieldNotes.bestTime: March to June; December to February for snow
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Fly to Bhuntar (Kullu) airport, or take an overnight bus from Delhi

photo.alt: The Golden Temple before dawn, reflected in the Amrit Sarovar

past.body: Amritsar is the spiritual heart of Sikhism. Harmandir Sahib sits on its sacred pool, the Amrit Sarovar. Pilgrims walk barefoot on cool marble around the sarovar, listening to live kirtan.

table.body: The langar is a community kitchen that serves free meals to everyone who visits, every single day. Try a stuffed Amritsari kulcha with chole, and a tall glass of lassi.

fieldNotes.body: Return after dark, when the gold reflects in the water and the crowds grow quiet.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Amritsar airport or Amritsar Junction railway station

past.body: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is a planned city of palaces and forts. The old city was painted terracotta pink, famously to welcome a royal visitor in 1876. Hawa Mahal is a honeycomb of small windows built so royal women could watch street life unseen.

table.body: Spend the evening in the old city bazaars, then try dal baati churma.

fieldNotes.body: Reach Amber Fort early to beat the heat and the crowds.

photo.alt: The Taj Mahal rising out of morning haze

past.body: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna, was a Mughal capital and is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Shah Jahan's white marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal changes colour with the light. Agra Fort is a red sandstone fortress of palaces, courtyards and marble pavilions.

table.body: Take home petha, and try bedai with jalebi for breakfast.

fieldNotes.body: Enter at opening time, and remember the Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Gatimaan Express or the Yamuna Expressway from Delhi

photo.alt: Blue hour on a Goan beach, shacks lighting up

past.body: Goa is India's smallest state, where Konkani, Portuguese and beach culture meet. Fontainhas is Panaji's Latin quarter of Portuguese-era houses. The Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral in Old Goa are part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

table.body: Goan fish curry is coconut, kokum and the catch of the day, served with rice. Finish every meal with bebinca, a layered coconut dessert.

fieldNotes.body: Head north for markets and nightlife, and south for quiet bays.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Dabolim or Mopa airport, Madgaon or Thivim station

photo.alt: Mist lifting off the tea slopes of Munnar

past.body: Munnar is a hill station in Kerala, named for the three mountain streams that meet among its tea estates. Tea bushes carpet the hills of the Western Ghats. Eravikulam National Park is home to the rare Nilgiri tahr and the neelakurinji flower that blooms once every twelve years.

table.body: Tea is still plucked by hand, two leaves and a bud at a time. Estate factories dry and roll the leaves; taste the difference at a tea museum.

fieldNotes.body: Take a guided walk through the tea rows in the cool morning mist.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Cochin airport, then about 3 to 4 hours by road

past.body: Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, clings to a ridge with views of Kanchenjunga, the world's third highest mountain. Rumtek is one of Sikkim's largest monasteries.

table.body: Steaming dumplings and noodle soup warm up every chilly evening.

fieldNotes.body: Arrive early at Rumtek or Enchey for morning prayers.
fieldNotes.bestTime: March to May, October to December
safety: Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La need permits, arranged through registered tour operators.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Pakyong airport, or Bagdogra airport and NJP station, then by road

photo.alt: The white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch under a full moon

past.body: The Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is one of the largest salt deserts in the world. Bhunga villages have round mud houses with conical roofs, decorated with mud and mirror work.

calendar.body: Rann Utsav is a winter festival of tents, folk music, dance and camel rides on the desert.

festivals.name: Rann Utsav
festivals.note: A winter festival of tents, folk music, dance and camel rides.

fieldNotes.body: Plan your visit around a full moon night.
safety: An entry permit is needed for the White Rann near Dhordo.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Bhuj airport or station, then by road to Dhordo

photo.alt: Afternoon rain rolling over the Khasi Hills

past.body: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, is known for its pine hills and colonial charm. Khasi communities guide rubber-tree roots across streams to grow living root bridges over many years.

table.body: Jadoh is Khasi rice cooked with meat and spices, sold at busy food stalls.

fieldNotes.body: Nearby Sohra is one of the wettest places on Earth, so pack a raincoat.
fieldNotes.gettingThere: Guwahati airport, then about 3 hours by road
